The Hedjaz Jordan Railway (Arabic: الخط الحديدي الحجازي الأردني, al-Khaṭṭ al-Ḥadīdī al-Ḥijāzī al-ʾUrdunī) is the section of the historic Hejaz Railway located in Jordan. It is a 1,050 mm (3 ft 7 in) narrow-gauge railway originally constructed by the Ottoman Empire to connect Damascus in Syria to Medina in present-day Saudi Arabia, facilitating the Hajj pilgrimage. The Jordanian portion spans approximately 452 km, though operational segments vary between passenger, freight, and heritage uses.[1]

Lyudi Invalidy (Russian: Люди Инвалиды, transl. Disabled People) is the second Russian-language studio album by the Russian duo t.A.T.u., released on 21 October 2005 by Interscope Records. It serves as the Russian counterpart to their international English-language album Dangerous and Moving, released earlier the same year. The album features Russian versions of most tracks from Dangerous and Moving, along with some English songs and an introductory track.[1]
